chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The pilgrim's burdens and his guarantee are upon Allah. So when he enters the Sacred Mosque, Allah appoints two angels to guard his circumambulation, his prayer, and his walking. When it is the evening of 'Arafah, they strike his right shoulder and say to him: 'O this one! As for what has passed, you have been spared from it; so see how you will be in what is to come.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a pilgrim's sins when he enters the Sacred Mosque and reaches 'Arafah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the metaphysical protection granted to the pilgrim, where Allah assumes the burden of his sins and physical needs. The specific ritual of the angels striking the right shoulder on the evening of 'Arafah symbolizes the transition from expiation of past sins to the responsibility of future conduct, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the spiritual climax of Hajj.
